results.title: Content ideas and pieces
results.summary: Phase 1 is built and all validation commands pass (632 tests). Step A moved the suite to Postgres (birdcar_test locally, pgvector service in CI) and fixed three real issues it exposed: a UTC pgsql session timezone, a key-order-insensitive check on protected blocks, and the Manual trial guard now requiring birdcar_test. Step B adds ContentIdea, PieceKind and a backfill migration, replaces capture() with captureIdea/addPiece/renameIdea, and shows ideas with a visible "Idea" label on every Admin surface, with inline rename in the workspace header. Spec deviations: content_ideas.author_id is nullable/nullOnDelete because the spec's FK combination would block user deletion, and the CI "Load published writing" step is left unchanged because it was already broken (ReadWriting::all does not exist). All 12 decisions are logged in implementation-notes-phase-1.html. — Step B matches the spec closely. ContentIdea, PieceKind, the migration with chunked backfill and a reversible down(), captureIdea/addPiece/renameIdea with authorization and transactions, removal of the Sluggable attribute, and every listed Blade/Livewire surface (now eager-loading contentIdea and rendering the summary only behind an 'Idea' label) are all in place. Tests are strong: derivation edge cases, rendered-HTML label assertions on all four surfaces, a raw-insert migration round-trip, and archive idempotency. Nothing blocks the commit, but before committing the Step A hunks should be split into their own commit, and the CI 'Load published writing' step (which calls a non-existent ReadWriting::all(), a problem that predates this change) should be verified or flagged.

results.title: Voice and goals canon in every prompt
results.summary: Replaced the per-post voice-sample checklist with a repo-owned voice and goals canon under resources/publishing/canon/: goals, core voice, 21 tagged mechanical rules, the blog channel, post types, 13 frameworks plus a guide, 9 role rubrics, roles.json and the exemplar manifest with a site-copy snapshot. A scoped VoiceCanon/CanonSnapshot service hashes the canon and builds its manifest version, StartEditorialActivity freezes the canon into every activity's input, EditorialAgent::instructions() renders the goals and rubric only from that frozen block, and activities created before the canon pause with the restart message without calling the provider. Also added publishing:canon-hash, removed all voice-sample code, reconciled PRODUCT.md, and wrote VoiceCanonTest and EditorialInputContractTest; every validation command passes (composer test: 674 tests). — The implementation closely follows the Phase 2 spec. VoiceCanon (scoped binding) and CanonSnapshot build a repo-relative sha256 manifest over the canon and the referenced archive sources. StartEditorialActivity freezes the canon per kind, EditorialAgent renders goals and rubric only from the frozen block, all voice-sample plumbing is gone (the grep sweep is clean), roles.json and the exemplar manifest match the spec, and all 21 rule ids are tagged exactly once. The new contract and canon tests cover every kind, live-canon change after freezing, path hygiene, the dashboard path and the pre-canon gate. The remaining findings are non-blocking: an undocumented pause-instead-of-fail deviation, a restart dead-end for pre-canon review rows that comes from review idempotency, and minor cleanups. The phase is ready to commit.
findings: medium/spec-deviation app/Actions/Publishing/RunEditorialActivity.php:77 — The spec's Error Handling and Testing Requirements say a pre-canon activity 'fails' with the restart message. The implementation pauses it instead: handleFailure routes a pre-invocation throw to pauseActivity, and EditorialInputContractTest asserts EditorialActivityStatus::Paused. The context map argues for this choice (a Failed row would offer a Retry that loops forever), but the spec text was never updated. → Keep the pause, and record the deviation in the phase implementation notes, or amend spec-phase-2.md so the spec and tests agree.

medium/logic app/Actions/Publishing/StartEditorialActivity.php:idempotencyPayload — For ReviewFacts, ReviewVoice, ReviewBuyer, Reconciliation and Recheck, the idempotency key leaves out prompt_hash. A paused pre-canon review row in the same cycle, batch key and revision is therefore returned again on 'restart', so 'Created before the voice canon; restart this step.' leads nowhere until the revision or cycle changes. Dev data has at least one such review_buyer row. → Either word the pause reason to say how to restart a review kind (for example, edit the draft or start a new review cycle), or make start() skip an existing row whose input lacks canon. Add a test covering the restart of a pre-canon review lens.

low/logic app/Ai/Agents/EditorialAgent.php:frozenCanon — RunEditorialActivity only checks that is_array(input.canon). A canon block with an empty or missing goals or rubric gets past that gate, then throws inside instructions() after $invoked = true. handleFailure then reports it as an uncertain provider outcome instead of the restart message. → Make the RunEditorialActivity gate check the same goals and rubric string conditions as frozenCanon(), so a malformed block also pauses before invocation.

low/spec-deviation app/Services/Publishing/CanonSnapshot.php:frozenFor — The frozen block adds a 'hash' key that duplicates 'version'; the spec's canon block has no such key. → Drop 'hash' (and its assertion in EditorialInputContractTest), or note why a second name for the same value is needed.

It also means a broken canon file returns a 500 for the whole workspace, not just for agent starts. → Acceptable for now. Consider catching RuntimeException and rendering 'Voice canon unavailable' so a canon error does not take down the editor.

results.title: Deterministic voice lint
results.summary: Built the deterministic voice lint. A tagged VoiceLinter runs 21 native PHP rules (one per canon [rule:] id) over a LintTarget. After a draft, the working revision is linted and up to two LintRepairer passes patch only blocks an agent wrote; anything left becomes blocking 'lint' findings and the review lenses queue. Owner saves re-lint through LintRevision. CheckArticleRelease blocks each hit as lint.<id> unless a reasoned override with the same hit hash exists. The workspace gained a "Voice rules" panel with Accept fix, Override with reason, and Skip repair and review. All validation passes: the spec's three test files (80 tests), Publishing (373), pint, PHPStan, and composer test (744). Spec deviations and owner decisions are logged in implementation-notes-phase-3.html: the bold-limit per-section reading, per-block agent authorship, and skipping archive essays. — PASS, cycle 2: all six cycle-1 findings are fixed, nothing was refuted, and the fixes introduce no new problems. (1) [FIXED] high/logic, LintRevision.php:350-401: currentPatch now compares hashes with the lock ignored (matchesIgnoringLock) and rebases a carried patch onto the block as it is now (new expected_hash, and withLockOf copies the block's current protected value). A protected hit's fix can now be accepted after the owner unlocks the block. ApplyEditorialProposal still refuses while the block is protected, and it skips the revision content-hash check only for the lint lens. (2) [FIXED] medium/testing, VoiceLintWorkflowTest.php:269: the test now unlocks the block, checks the carried patch has protected=false, accepts it, and asserts the patched text, an unlocked block, disposition 'accepted' and no open findings. (3) [FIXED] medium/logic, RunEditorialActivity.php finishLintAfterUnusableRepair: the unusable repair is now marked Stale with an error_reason. The test at :430 confirms RetryEditorialActivity refuses it and 'Skip repair and review' no longer shows. (4) [FIXED] low/logic, VoiceLinter.php:40: repeated identical hits are now numbered by occurrence (LintHit::withOccurrence), so they hash apart, with a dataset test at VoiceLintTest.php:234. The renumbering trade-off is written up in the implementation notes. (5) [FIXED] low/spec-deviation, RunEditorialActivity.php agentWrittenBlockHashes: each block now keeps the hash from its latest agent write, matching the spec's 'most recent agent-initial or agent-repair revision'. A test covers an owner restoring earlier agent text. (6) [FIXED] low/spec-deviation, BoldLimit.php: the implementation notes now record the choice to follow the canon over the spec's rule table, with a bold-limit entry and an overview for the acceptance review of the word lists. Per the reviewer's git-only Bash rule, I did not run the test suite. The phase is ready to commit once the spec's validation commands pass.

results.title: Exemplar retrieval
results.summary: Built Phase 5 exemplar retrieval: the pgvector table and HNSW index, the openrouter-embeddings provider (now the embeddings default), the section indexer, a publish job and a backfill command. Blog-post plan approvals retrieve the closest sections before the transaction, but only when agents are unpaused. Draft and ReviewVoice freeze them as canon.retrieved_exemplars; the reviewer copies the Draft's sections. All spec validation commands pass (composer test: 759 tests, Pint and PHPStan clean). Three things for the owner. (1) The Laravel Cloud docs say Serverless Postgres supports pgvector, but read-only CLI checks could not confirm production has a Postgres database attached, so confirm it before deploy. (2) The safety classifier stopped me partway through writing the context map, so context-map.md was left at its Phase 3 content and not updated. (3) 10 decisions, including a new shared ExemplarEmbeddings service not named in the spec, are logged in implementation-notes-phase-5.html. — The implementation follows the spec. It adds the openrouter-embeddings provider as the embeddings default, a pgvector migration with no driver guard and an HNSW cosine index, hash-keyed indexing that upserts, prunes and embeds in batches of 64, retrieval computed before the approval transaction with an unavailable fallback, and Draft/ReviewVoice freezing (ReviewVoice copies its Draft's sections). Departures from the spec are recorded in the Phase 5 notes and none goes against the decision log: LintTarget instead of documentText, a shared ExemplarEmbeddings service, and pause gating. Tests cover eligibility, chunking, idempotency, the outbound request shape, the no-api.openai.com assertion, transaction level, failure paths, the publish hook, the command, and the pgvector index and ordering. I did not run the test suite because this review was limited to read-only git commands. The four findings are all low severity, so this is ready to commit once the doc artifacts are sorted out.
findings: low/logic app/Actions/Publishing/ApprovePublishingStage.php:43 — Retrieval runs before the stale-hash check (line 50) and ensureApprovalIsAllowed(). A stale or disallowed plan approval still makes the paid embeddings call and waits up to the 15s retrieval timeout before it throws. → Before calling exemplarContextFor(), run the same cheap checks on an unlocked fresh attempt: inputHashFor() compared with $expectedInputHash, plus ensureApprovalIsAllowed(). Keep the authoritative checks inside the transaction.

No test covers it, and the `none` status is covered only indirectly by EditorialInputContractTest. → Add a case: approve the plan, rethink the plan argument, start a Draft. Assert retrieval_status 'stale' and an empty retrieved_exemplars.

results.title: Frameworks, sharper reviewers and packaging
results.summary: Phase 4 is built. The canon gains a frameworks/catalog.json, a metadata-rules canon file and a packager rubric; FrameworkCatalog validates Planner proposals; the plan gate offers a framework choice that can trigger a re-plan; the Draft and VoiceReviewer receive the chosen framework and post-type text frozen in full; the three lens rubrics carry section markers; a new Package activity and Packager agent run after review, and AcceptPackageProposal saves the owner's accepted package as a metadata-only revision; five metadata lint rules run at packaging and release; and release approval now uses a single lineage, so a metadata-only package revision keeps its review coverage, while the release payload carries a claim_manifest. Every validation command passes (composer test: 827 tests). context-map.md was not rewritten with the Phase 4 map: the write was interrupted. Gap decisions are logged in implementation-notes-phase-4.html. — Phase 4 matches the spec closely. FrameworkCatalog follows the VoiceCanon read-from-snapshot pattern and freezes the catalog into Interview/Plan inputs. The plan gate stores chosen inside the hashed plan, and re-plans use plan-{cycle}-{slug}. The metadata lint rules are implemented once and shared by package validation and CheckArticleRelease. reviewLineage now treats metadata-only revisions as reviewed and replaces the duplicated recheck logic in ManageArticleRelease. The claim manifest is included in the release hash. Tests cover every spec experiment. There are no blocking findings; the two medium items (the nullable enum, and the title not being checked against the options) should be fixed when convenient, and the change is ready to commit.
findings: medium/logic app/Ai/Agents/EditorialAgent.php:214 — Interview `postType` is built as `string()->enum([...])->nullable()`. The Laravel JsonSchema serializer turns that into `{"type":["string","null"],"enum":["essay","playbook","teardown","work_story"]}`. Null is not in the enum, so a schema-validating or strict provider either rejects null or forces the model to pick a type. That contradicts interviewer.md ("Use null only when the answers so far genuinely cannot tell") and the null-handling in validateInterview/applyInterview. → Add null to the enum values, or drop the enum and rely on the description plus EditorialOutput::validateInterview. Add a schema assertion in NarrativeFrameworkTest showing that null is representable.

medium/logic app/Services/Publishing/EditorialOutput.php:validatePackage — The schema says `title` is 'chosen from titleOptions', but validation never checks that the chosen H1 is one of the ten options. A Packager can return a title outside its own choice set, which defeats the 'ten options first, then pick' rubric the spec describes. → Reject a package whose trimmed `title` does not match one of the trimmed titleOptions (case-insensitive, as in the distinctness check), give a reason that names the mismatch, and add a PackagingTest dataset row.

low/spec-deviation resources/publishing/canon/frameworks/catalog.json:avoid_combinations — The spec's catalog lists four avoid pairs, including ["reverse-chronology", "kishotenketsu"]. The implementation keeps three. Dropping the pair is defensible, since kishotenketsu is not one of the 13 frameworks in guide.md, but the drop is undocumented. → Restore the pair (fromArray does not require avoid slugs to be catalog frameworks) or record why it was dropped in the phase implementation notes.

low/spec-deviation resources/publishing/canon/roles.json:draft — The draft role now freezes voice/metadata-rules.md, and the Draft `document` schema description still tells the Drafter it must pass every VoiceLinter rule id, including seo-title-length, slug-shape and the other metadata rules. The spec has the Drafter stop proposing metadata, so this sends mixed signals; it appears to exist only so the Phase 3 two-way prompt check passes. → Either limit the Draft document description to body/character rule ids and adjust the two-way check to cover the package prompt for metadata rules, or keep it and note the reason in implementation notes.

low/logic app/Actions/Publishing/FinishEditorialReview.php:staleEarlierPackages — A Running package is excluded from staling. It can still complete after a recheck starts, and the workspace's latestPackage() then shows it until the post-recheck package completes, even though AcceptPackageProposal will refuse it. → Have latestPackage() skip packages older than the latest recheck of the cycle, or mark a package stale in applyResult when a newer recheck exists.

results.title: Distribution kit and sibling pieces
results.summary: Approving a flagship blog post's release now creates three kit pieces (LinkedIn, Bluesky, email). Each piece is drafted by KitDrafter, goes through the existing lint and self-repair loop, and is then checked by KitReviewer, which blocks on claims outside the release's claim manifest. The owner approves a piece with the new ApprovalKind::Kit, copies it out from a compact kit panel, and marks it posted only once the flagship is live. The phase also adds nine canon-tagged kit lint rules, CreateSiblingPiece (the interview gets sibling_context), a 'New post from this idea' button, a posted_at/posted_url migration, and a filter that keeps kit pieces out of public writing readers. All validation commands pass: kit/sibling/lint tests 110/110, the publishing suite 511/511, Pint, PHPStan with 0 errors, and composer test 882/882. Judgment calls, including the decision to keep every kit field as a document block instead of in metadata, are recorded in implementation-notes-phase-6.html. — The phase 6 work matches the spec: enums, migration, kit canon and roles.json, nine kit lint rules with a two-way id check, KitDrafter/KitReviewer on different model families, idempotent spawning that restarts unapproved pieces, kit approval gating, the Posted-after-live rule, siblings with sibling_context, and public readers filtered to blog posts. Tests cover every spec experiment (a) through (f). No critical or high findings, so it is commit-ready. Three medium issues should still be fixed soon: an owner who edited a piece before a restart can only approve by discarding those edits, 'I fixed it' clears a blocking claim finding with no edit or reason, and the approval exemption trusts a piece_kind value that callers can supply.
findings: medium/logic app/Actions/Publishing/ApprovePublishingStage.php:207 — Approving a kit needs a completed review_kit in the current review_cycle. SpawnDistributionKit::restart (SpawnDistributionKit.php:199) bumps review_cycle, and when the owner has edited the piece, applyDraftKit stores the new draft as a proposal, so lintThenQueueReviews never queues review_kit. ensureReviewKitEligible also refuses a revision the owner wrote. The owner can then never approve their own edited text; the only way out is 'Replace my text with this draft', which throws their edits away. That contradicts the 'never replaces the owner's words' intent → Give the owner a path to review their current revision against the new flagship release. Either allow review_kit on the working revision when the cycle has a waiting (unapplied) draft_kit, or add a 'Keep my text and review it' action that queues review_kit for the owner revision. Add a DistributionKitTest case covering it.

medium/logic app/Actions/Publishing/ApprovePublishingStage.php:241 — decideKitFinding accepts 'accepted' ('I fixed it') on a blocking claim_outside_manifest finding with no reason and no check that the text changed. One click clears the claim gate without an edit or a recorded justification, which weakens the contract decision that kit pieces may not add claims outside the manifest → For a blocking finding, allow 'accepted' only when the working revision differs from the finding's reviewed revision (or require a reason). Add a test.

medium/security app/Actions/Publishing/StartEditorialActivity.php:990 — prerequisiteApproval decides whether an activity is exempt from angle/plan approval checks by reading input['piece_kind']. pieceContext (line 291) only forces piece_kind for kit articles, so a blog-post activity started with caller input ['piece_kind' => 'linkedin_post'] keeps that value through array_merge. activityMatchesCurrentApproval and RunEditorialActivity::staleReason then skip the approval check. Every current caller builds its input internally, so this is not exploitable today, but the pieceContext docblock claims 'no caller can forge it' → In pieceContext, always set 'piece_kind' => $article->kind->value (or unset any caller-supplied piece_kind for blog posts), so the frozen value always comes from the article.

low/spec-deviation app/Services/Publishing/KitDocument.php:FIELDS — The spec Data Model says kit revisions keep subject, preview and first_comment in metadata. The implementation keeps every field only as a document paragraph. The deviation is documented and justified in implementation-notes-phase-6.html: metadata hits have no block id and could not be repaired → No code change needed. Update the spec's Data Model line, or confirm the deviation with the owner, so later phases (Phase 7 board/copy-out) do not read metadata.

low/logic app/Actions/Publishing/SpawnDistributionKit.php:137 — useDraft goes straight to finishAndQueueReviews, so an owner-accepted kit draft skips the lint self-repair loop that a draft landing on its own gets. Its revision origin 'agent-accepted' is also not treated as agent-written by applyDraftKit on a later restart. The docblock says it is 'linted and reviewed like any draft that landed on its own' → Either route it through the same lint-then-repair path, or correct the docblock to say repair is skipped.

low/logic app/Actions/Publishing/MarkKitPiecePosted.php:mark — Unmet posting conditions throw RuntimeException. The spec's Error Handling table says 'Validation error naming the unmet condition'. The UI surfaces the message either way → Throw ValidationException::withMessages(['posted_url' => $problem]) or similar, to match the spec and the postedUrl error binding.

low/logic app/Actions/Publishing/ApprovePublishingStage.php:kitApprovalProblems — A kit piece can be approved while its frozen flagship release no longer stands (withdrawn or edited after approval). The panel only shows a warning → Consider adding a problem line when the frozen flagship release no longer stands approved, so the owner cannot approve a piece cut from a withdrawn release.

low/spec-deviation resources/publishing/canon/channels/kit.md:25 — The channel canon says to number every post i/n 'at its start'. voice/kit-rules.md and BlueskyNumbering accept start or end → Align the two canon files, for example 'at its start (the linter also accepts the end)'.

results.title: Drift trial harness and edit distance
results.summary: Phase 9 is built, and every validation command passed. It adds the drift golden set (passages.json, a shared DriftGoldenSet builder, DriftFixtureTest) and a paid trial, VoiceDriftTrialTest, that skips unless DRIFT_TRIAL=1 is set. It also adds edit-distance measurement: an EditDistance service, a RecordEditDistance job dispatched after commit from WriteArticle::save, nullable columns that can be set once, and the publishing:edit-distances command. VoiceReviewer finding kinds (voice_drift, clarity, framework, register) are now an enforced schema enum, checked by the validator and defined in the rubric. Decisions are logged in implementation-notes-phase-9.html: passages are linted without walkthrough-link, four slopped passages carry no mechanical tell, and autosave keeps most recorded edit distances to a few words. — The implementation follows spec-phase-9 closely. The edit-distance math correctly uses two rows and trims shared opening and closing words. The job is queued after commit only when an owner save follows an agent revision, and it does nothing on a second run. The command's JSON is a superset of the spec's shape. The paid trial follows the PublishingModelTrialTest pattern: it refuses to run unless isolated, uses driftTrial-prefixed helpers, records every attempt without retries, and writes fields the contract's jq check can read. Two things should be fixed but don't block: the golden set marks every slopped block as injected, so the injected-span check proves nothing; and the guard does not enforce that only the job writes the two columns. With no critical or high findings, this phase is ready to commit.
findings: medium/testing tests/Fixtures/Publishing/drift/passages.json:slopped — Every block of every slopped passage has an injected tell. slop-04, slop-05 and slop-10 have one block, and the other seven mark both of their blocks. So `caught_at_injected_span` (VoiceDriftTrialTest.php:228-231) only asks whether any lint hit or any finding with a block_id exists, and the contract's "flag at the injected span" test (G3) cannot fail on location. Also, 6 of the 10 are caught by lint every time because they carry mechanical tells. → Leave at least one block untagged in each multi-block slopped variant, either by keeping it close to the real wording or by adding a clean block. Then add a DriftFixtureTest assertion that every multi-block slopped passage has at least one block without an injected tell, so where a finding lands actually matters.

medium/spec-deviation app/Models/ArticleRevision.php:49-57 — The spec says the guard lets the two columns be set once from null, and only from the job. The guard lets any caller that loaded the columns set them once; EditDistanceTest.php:819 does this outside the job. The job itself skips the guard by using a query-builder update (RecordEditDistance.php:170-173). "Only from the job" is a docblock convention and nothing enforces it. → Enforce it: for example, a dedicated `ArticleRevision::recordEditDistance()` that only the job calls, with the updating guard rejecting any other model write to these columns. Otherwise, get the spec changed to say "set once from null" and drop "only from the job".

low/logic app/Jobs/RecordEditDistance.php:144 — `SerializesModels` is unused because the job carries only an int revision id. → Drop the trait unless the existing job pattern (IndexPublishedExemplar) keeps it on purpose.

low/spec-deviation app/Actions/Publishing/WriteArticle.php:157-159 — This follows the spec, but the editor autosaves after 250 ms idle. The recorded distance therefore covers only the owner's first burst of typing after an agent revision, so G6 values will be close to zero. The builder flagged this in the phase-9 notes. → Raise it with the owner as a contract open item before the acceptance gate rather than changing it in this phase.

They could be left out of the phase commit. → Register the phase-9 notes so they ship with this phase.

results.title: Publishing board
results.summary: Built the Phase 7 publishing board, which replaces the dashboard at /publishing and keeps the route name and the composer. It has ten columns derived from each piece's stage, flags and activities (BoardColumn); kit pieces nest inside their flagship card as chips; status chips show running, waiting or failed (PieceStatus); the board polls every 10 seconds; and drags and a matching card menu go through MovePublishingPiece/MoveResult. Allowed moves: Ideas→Shaping starts development and the interview; Ready→Scheduled hands off to the workspace release checklist; Parked and Killed open a reason modal; Parked→own column unparks via a new AdvancePublishingAttempt::unpark(). Every other move is refused with a message naming the gate. Choices the spec didn't settle or conflicted with: park and kill authorize develop (the spec says write, but the existing action requires develop); park and kill withdraw any scheduled release; unpark requeues work a worker paused before calling the provider; refusals show in an in-board alert because the layout has no toast. These and the other choices are in implementation-notes-phase-7.html. The dashboard tests were rewritten to target the board, not deleted. All validation commands pass, including composer test with 995 tests. No interactive drag was tried in a browser; the owner's manual review is still to do. — The implementation follows the spec and the context map closely: columns are derived from stage, moves are checked server-side with a lock and re-derived, a card menu repeats the allowed moves for touch screens, nested kit chips, a query-count test across 3 and 30 cards, and the dashboard tests are rewritten rather than deleted, with the changes from the spec recorded in the implementation notes. No critical or high findings. The main medium issues are in what parking leaves behind: a Scheduled piece parked and then unparked ends up Scheduled with a withdrawn release, unpark requeues too many paused activities, and the board's open-findings rule has drifted from the Admin home's. Ready to commit; those three are worth fixing first or right after.
findings: medium/logic app/Actions/Publishing/MovePublishingPiece.php:217 — Parking a Scheduled piece withdraws its release but leaves the attempt at stage Scheduled. When it is unparked, BoardColumn::forStage returns it to the Scheduled column ("Waiting for its time") even though nothing is scheduled and publishing:publish-due will never deliver it. → When setAside withdraws a scheduled release on park, also move the stage back to Approved so an unpark lands in Ready. Otherwise refuse parking Scheduled pieces and tell the owner to withdraw from the workspace first. Add a test for park, then unpark, on a Scheduled piece.

medium/logic app/Actions/Publishing/AdvancePublishingAttempt.php:423 — unpark requeues every activity on the attempt that is Paused with BLOCKED_ATTEMPT_PAUSE_REASON. That includes activities a worker paused during an earlier attempt pause (resume() never revives this reason) and activities already superseded by a newer activity of the same kind. Unparking can therefore re-run outdated agent work and pay for it. → Limit the update to activities paused while this park was active (paused_at >= the attempt's parked_at, captured before clearing it). Also skip rows that have a newer activity of the same kind on the attempt. Add a test with an activity blocked before the park that must stay Paused.

medium/logic app/Services/Publishing/BoardColumn.php:596 — has_open_findings drops ReadAdminHome's condition that the finding sits on the working revision with a matching content_hash (ReadAdminHome.php:53-55), and adds severity = blocking. The board's "Decide the open findings" chip and the Admin home's "Your decision" list can now disagree about the same piece. PieceStatus says it mirrors the Admin home. → Share one definition between ReadAdminHome and BoardColumn::withAttemptFlags, or add the working-revision/content-hash constraint here. Make the test fixture's input_hash match its revision.

low/performance resources/views/components/admin/publishing/⚡board.blade.php:165 — The Ideas and Killed columns have no cap. Killed is fully queried and rendered on every 10-second poll even while collapsed, so poll cost grows with every piece the owner has ever killed. The implementation notes record this choice. → Consider loading Killed cards only when the column is expanded, or capping it with a count and a link, the same way Published is capped.

low/spec-deviation resources/views/components/admin/publishing/⚡board.blade.php:303 — wire:poll.10s.visible sits on the cards region but re-renders the whole component, including the composer and the reason modal. Spec step 5 asks for polling limited to the cards region. The implementation notes record that islands were rejected. → Acceptable as recorded. Check in the browser that text typed in the composer and the modal survives a poll that is in flight, or move the poll into an @island.

low/spec-deviation resources/views/components/admin/publishing/⚡board.blade.php:334 — Only the heading link opens the workspace. Clicking anywhere else on the card body does nothing, but the spec says "Clicking a card opens the workspace." → Make the whole card body the link target (for example a stretched-link overlay below the menu and kit chips), keeping wire:sort:ignore on the inner controls.

low/security resources/views/components/admin/publishing/⚡board.blade.php:218 — titleFor, ideaHasMoreThanItsSummary and targetLabel are public methods, so the client can call them through $wire, and Livewire's implicit model binding resolves an Article id passed to them. The risk is limited because with() authorizes on every request and this pattern was copied from the deleted dashboard. → Make the helpers protected/private, or compute the values in card() so the view never calls component methods with an Article.

low/testing tests/Feature/Publishing/PublishingBoardTest.php:254 — Nothing tests that a sibling blog post (created with CreateSiblingPiece, which sets no parent) gets its own top-level card and does not nest under the flagship. → Add a case with a flagship, one sibling and one kit, and assert two cards and one nested chip.

low/testing tests/Feature/Publishing/PublishingBoardTest.php:597 — The test name 'loads thirty pieces in no more queries than three' reads as "at most three queries". The test actually asserts that the query count with 30 cards equals the count with 3 cards and is at most 30. → Rename it to something like 'the board's query count stays flat from three to thirty pieces'.
